Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the UniBank Holdings third quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review UniBank Holdings's results for the third quarter. With me this morning are David Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Emily Carter, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Reynolds, Chief Risk Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Credit Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to David Thompson.

David Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. UniBank Holdings delivered strong performance in the third quarter, driven by our commitment to customer service and operational excellence.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Growing our core businesses
2. Investing in technology and innovation
3. Managing risk effectively
4. Optimizing our capital allocation
5. Enhancing our employee engagement.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on key areas of focus. First, fee income showed impressive resilience, with broad-based growth across wealth management, investment banking, and cards, totaling $2.8 billion, up 14% year-over-year, representing 28% of total revenue—our strongest quarterly result since late 2021. Wealth management led with $1.25 billion, up 18%, on record assets under management and strong net new money. Investment banking fees hit $950 million, up 12%, bolstered by solid M&A advisory and debt capital markets. Cards added $650 million, up 9%, from higher transaction volumes and rewards program uptake.

Second, operating expenses were well-controlled at $2.48 billion, up just 4.2% year-over-year on an adjusted basis, improving our efficiency ratio to 58.2%, as we balanced investments in technology with cost discipline through attrition, offshoring, and branch optimization.

Third, our net interest margin expanded to 3.42%, up 12 basis points sequentially, thanks to higher earning asset yields, favorable mix shifts, and disciplined deposit betas, outperforming many peers.

Fourth, provisions for credit losses came in at $425 million, reflecting prudent CECL reserving amid uneven economic signals, with reserves at 1.45% of loans and strong coverage of charge-offs.

Fifth, deposit costs rose modestly to 3.87% on average balances of $285 billion, managed effectively against intense competition through dynamic pricing and retention strategies.

These results underscore our diversified model and strategic execution. I will now turn the call over to Emily Carter to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Emily Carter:
Thank you, David, and good morning. UniBank Holdings reported net income of $1.5 billion for the third quarter, or $3.20 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 10% year-over-year due to loan growth and an improved net interest margin. Non-interest income rose 14%, driven by the fee franchises David highlighted. Key performance indicators include a return on tangible equity of 13.2% and a CET1 ratio of 11.8%. We are confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Let me unpack our fee income performance in more detail, as it's a cornerstone of our diversified revenue stream and proved resilient amid macroeconomic headwinds. Non-interest income from fees reached $2.8 billion, up 14% from last year and 5% from the prior quarter, making up 28% of total revenue—our best since Q4 2021. This was propelled by our three main areas: wealth management, investment banking, and cards, accounting for 92% of the total.

Wealth management generated $1.25 billion, or 45% of fees, surging 18% year-over-year. Assets under management hit a record $1.7 trillion, up 12%, with $45 billion in net new money mainly from high-net-worth individuals and family offices. Equity market gains, like the S&P 500's 15% year-to-date rise, and 22% appreciation in our alternatives via the UniBank Alternatives platform fueled this. North America delivered 55% of inflows from strong ties with ultra-high-net-worth clients in the tri-state area, cross-selling our Signature Banking alongside advisory. EMEA inflows jumped 25% to €20 billion, recovering from prior outflows, with ESG products now at 18% of AUM, up from 12%, to meet EU SFDR rules. In Asia-Pacific, our Temasek partnership targets 20% growth via Singapore and Hong Kong for RMB flows. Average fee rates expanded 200 basis points to 75 bps, from performance fees and custody growth on our AuA platform at $450 billion. Our UniWealth AI tool, using machine learning for personalized advice, lifted retention to 96% and digital use to 65% among 2.5 million clients. We're committing $500 million more to evergreen private equity funds to tap the $10 trillion alternatives market.

Investment banking fees totaled $950 million, 34% of the mix, up 12%, with a strong pipeline despite M&A volatility. We're ranked #4 in global M&A advisory by Dealogic, with $150 billion in volume, and #3 in ECM. Advisory, 55% of fees, grew 16% on deals like a $25 billion LBO for Apollo's industrials carve-out and a $12 billion pharma-biotech merger. Debt markets shone, up 25% to $350 million, as IG spreads hit 120 bps post-Fed pause, with $80 billion in high-yield at 8.5% blended yield. ECM grew 5%, held back by IPO timing, but shelf deals with tech unicorns set up 2024 gains. U.S. drove 60%, with TMT and healthcare coverage boosting bulge-bracket share; APAC 20% from China reopening and Korean restructurings; Europe flat but with €50 billion ECM pipeline. Our originate-to-distribute approach sourced 40% from 5,000 CIB clients. Investments in quantum-secure data rooms and ESG tools won deals, and we're growing infrastructure advisory—$100 billion pipeline tied to IRA and EU Green Deal—for 15% fee growth next year.

Cards and payments fees reached $650 million, 23% of total, up 9%, on steady consumer spending despite inflation. Interchange grew 11%, with 1.2 billion swipes, up 8%, via UniCard Rewards for 15 million accounts, including crypto cashback with Binance. Average ticket rose 4% to $85, redemptions to 72% via ML personalization. International up 20% from Visa/Mastercard in LATAM and Alipay remittances. U.S. (70% volume) gained from travel like Delta ties; EMEA 15% on contactless; China pivoting to B2B virtual cards. Tokenization on blockchain cut fraud 30% for premium cards and enables fintech APIs like Plaid. BNPL expansions target the $1 trillion U.S. market, guiding 12% growth next year.

Overall, these areas delivered $2.58 billion, with margins up 150 bps to 45% from scale and $1.2 billion tech spend. We anticipate mid-teens growth ahead with market support, M&A recovery, and consumer strength.

Turning to operating expenses, our non-interest expenses totaled $2.48 billion, up 4.2% year-over-year and 1.8% quarter-over-quarter. Stripping out a $85 million one-time regulatory charge for legacy AML systems—similar to peer actions—adjusted expenses were $2.395 billion, up 2.1%, holding our efficiency ratio at 58.2%, down 110 basis points year-over-year and on track for mid-50s.

Compensation and benefits, 42% of total at $1.04 billion, rose 3.8%, from 2.5% merit pay and incentives linked to fee gains. Headcount at 48,200 FTEs was flat quarter-over-quarter, up 1.2% with 250 tech/data hires for AI customer platforms, offset by attrition and 15% offshoring to Manila/Hyderabad, saving $45 million annually like Wells Fargo's efforts.

Tech and data processing, 22% at $545 million, grew 12%, from $1.2 billion CapEx including Temenos cloud for 12 million U.S. deposit accounts. Gen AI for fraud cut false positives 28%, like Capital One's tools; Swift GPI blockchain sped APAC payments. Cybersecurity up 18% to $120 million post-ransomware events.

Occupancy flat at $210 million, up 0.5%, via closing 45 branches in Midwest and digital wallets with Walmart/Target boosting deposits 15% cost-free.

Professional fees, 18% at $446 million, up 6% for Basel IV modeling—$300 million CET1 boost expected—and stress testing. Marketing up 8% to $140 million for "Banking Reimagined" pushing 4.5% HYSA.

U.S. (55% OpEx) up 3%, helped by Fiserv hub; Europe (25%) up 7% for PSD3/Brexit but ratio to 62%; Asia (15%) flat with digital lifts like WeChat/Grab.

Our "Efficiency Everywhere" targets $500 million savings by 2025 via zero-based budgeting, RPA on 40% loan workflows, and vendor deals saving 12% with FIS. Q3 growth guided at 2-3%, with $60 million AI gains vs. 3.5% wage inflation. Revenue outpacing expenses supports 12% ROTE in 2025.

Next, our net interest margin of 3.42% rose 12 basis points from Q2's 3.30% and 25 basis points year-over-year—third straight quarter of gains, beating KBW peers by 18 basis points.

Earning asset yields up 28 bps to 5.18%, offset by 16 bps higher funds cost to 1.76%; net spot gain 8 bps plus mix shifts. Fed hike flowed to variable loans.

Loans (68% assets) yields up 32 bps to 5.65%; C&I (42%) new at SOFR+285 bps vs. +245; CRE multifamily grew 4%; consumer auto 6.8%, warehouse compressed.

Securities (22%) up 15 bps to 4.25%; duration cut to 3.8 years, $2.5 billion into 4.9% Agency MBS/corporates, adding 10 bps YTD, HQLA >110%.

Deposits grew 3% to $285 billion; core non-interest DDA/NOW 32%, beta 42% overall—checking 25%, CDs 65%. Time deposits 18% at 3.85% new, capped 5% growth. Wholesale to 4.95%, but only 8% funding.

Southeast NIM 3.65% on wealth referrals; Europe 2.95% mitigated by U.S. shifts.

Dynamic pricing with FIS/Temenos cut CD rates 15 bps; SOFR futures hedged 40% beta at 35%, saving 5 bps. Blend platform boosted C&I yields 30 bps. Target 10-15% variable CRE/equipment growth.

NIM to rise 5-10 bps Q4 to 3.47-3.52%; 2024 trough Q1 then 3.50%+ with 6-8% loans.

On provisions for credit losses, we recorded $425 million, up 18% from Q2's $360 million and 42% year-over-year, prudently under CECL. Coverage 1.25x charge-offs; reserves $8.2 billion, 1.45% of loans, up 10 bps.

Loans $450 billion: consumer (45%, $202B) $180M provision, delinquencies 1.8%; cards 2.9%, autos 0.9%; charge-offs $120M at 65 bps; $25M overlay.

CRE (25%, $112B) $210M, office criticized 15% on vacancies; multifamily 1.2% NPLs; charge-offs $80M from restructurings.

C&I (20%, $90B) $25M, delinquencies 1.1%; SBA strong.

Other $10M leases.

Charge-offs $340M (75 bps), delinquencies 1.95%.

Drivers: CECL scenarios—base 65% weight (4.1% GDP, 4.2% UE), adverse 25%, severe 10%; $75M overlay CRE/cards. Rates pressured refis; criticized 4.2%. Derisked $2.5B office sale.

Southeast low delinqs 1.4%; Midwest higher.

Methodology: PD/LGD/EAD x 1,200 segments; ML models cut error 12%; Plaid data early warning 20%; downturn LGD floors.

Sensitivity: +100 bps Fed $200M PCL; soft landing -$150M.

CRE coverage 120%; pivot industrial/data centers. Q4 $400-450M.

Finally, cost of deposits averaged 3.87%, up 12 bps quarter-over-quarter on $285 billion balances, up 2.1%; 248 bps YoY. Beta 78%, like peers, below PNC.

Savings/MM 42% at 4.12%, up 18 bps vs. Ally/SoFi; CDs 12% 4.45%; NIB 18% at 0.15%.

Pressures: Midwest locals >4.3%; South neobanks; MMFs $6.5T AUM siphoned $120B. JPM beta 75%.

AI pricing scraped competitors; Q2 "Deposit Shield" retained 92%; de-emphasized brokered <2%. Midwest 2.85%, Southeast 4.25%.

Q4 up 5-8 bps, peak Q1 4.05% then down post-cuts. LDR 78%, LCR 145%.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Emily. As Chief Risk Officer, I would like to briefly discuss our risk management framework. We continue to prioritize proactive risk identification and mitigation. Our key focus areas include credit migration in CRE office segments, cybersecurity amid rising threats, deposit beta volatility, operational resilience in payments, and emerging geopolitical risks in APAC/EMEA. We remain vigilant in monitoring emerging risks like prolonged yield curve inversion and inflation persistence, adapting strategies with enhanced CECL overlays, AI early warnings, and stress testing aligned to CCAR. Our CET1 buffer and HQLA position us strongly.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, instructions for queuing up. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the fee income growth drivers, particularly outlook for investment banking into next year?

David Thompson:
Good morning, John. Happy to elaborate. As Emily detailed, the growth was broad-based, but IB's 12% rise to $950 million stemmed from executing on a robust pipeline despite M&A choppiness—strong league table positions in advisory and ECM, standout debt markets with HY issuances, and regional momentum in U.S./APAC. Strategically, originate-to-distribute, tech investments like quantum data rooms, and infrastructure push give us confidence for 15% growth in FY25 as M&A normalizes and equity tailwinds continue, building on our €50 billion Europe pipeline and tech unicorn shelves.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
What are your expectations for NIM trajectory into 2025 given deposit competition?

Emily Carter:
Thanks, Mike. Our 3.42% NIM benefited from asset repricing and deposit discipline this quarter. Looking ahead, we see 5-10 bps more expansion in Q4 to 3.47-3.52%, then stabilizing above 3.50% in 2024 full-year, supported by 6-8% loan growth in variable-rate areas and mix shifts. Into 2025, post-Fed cuts, betas should unwind faster downward, with hedges and dynamic pricing capping peaks. Risks like curve delays noted, but 85% LDR and capital give flexibility—well ahead of peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Keefe Bruyette. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee:
Can you comment on the credit quality of the CRE portfolio, especially office?

Lisa Patel:
Good morning, Sarah. Credit quality remains solid overall, with reserves at 1.45% and strong coverage. CRE drove much of the $425 million provision, particularly office where criticized loans hit 15% amid high vacancies in metros like NYC/SF—similar to industry trends. We've derisked via $2.5 billion sales, shifted to Sun Belt multifamily/industrial, and curtailed new office to under 5% of pipeline. ML models and overlays position us prudently, with 120% coverage vs. peers' 100%, targeting data center growth with hyperscalers.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to David Thompson for any closing remarks.

David Thompson:
Thank you for your interest in UniBank Holdings. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
